title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700
gist: Apple's 8th-gen iPad mini starts at $699 (up from a $499 launch price in 2024 and $599 since), moving to an 8.5-inch OLED display, a 2nm A20 Pro chip, IP67 rating and a 5.4 mm body. Lower-storage models get a cut-down CPU and a single Neural Engine, tiering on-device AI capability by price.

insights.claim: The 8th-gen iPad mini starts at $699 for 128GB Wi-Fi, versus a $499 launch price for the 7th-gen model in 2024 that later rose to $599, marking another Apple price increase.
insights.so_what: Apple continues to push ASPs higher across its lineup, supporting revenue per unit.
insights.quote: Pricing is, sadly, not eye-popping for 2026, but it marks yet another price increase for Apple.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: The iPad mini's 256GB tier costs $100 more and 512GB $300 more than base, the nano-texture display is a $100 upsell limited to 256GB/512GB, and cellular starts at $849 for 128GB.
insights.so_what: Feature gating to higher storage tiers is a deliberate mix-shift lever for margins.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: Preorders for the new iPad mini begin October 28 with availability on November 6.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: The new iPad mini moves from IPS to an 8.5-inch OLED Super Retina XDR display (up from 8.3 inches) with 1,200 nits peak brightness versus 500 nits previously and a 1-nit minimum, enabled by a 24 percent bezel reduction.
insights.so_what: OLED continues to spread down Apple's product stack, expanding demand for OLED panel suppliers.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: The 8th-gen iPad mini is 5.4 mm thin, nearly a millimeter thinner than before, and gains an IP67 water and dust rating that the 7th-gen lacked.
insights.so_what: Apple calls it the most significant iPad mini update ever, a potential upgrade catalyst.
insights.locator: The new iPad mini has roughly
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: The iPad mini jumps from a 3nm A17 Pro, already a year old at its launch, to the 2nm A20 Pro, which in the iPhone 18 Pro significantly improved graphics thanks partly to a 50 percent increase in memory bandwidth.
insights.so_what: Faster adoption of leading-edge 2nm silicon across devices supports foundry demand at the leading node.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: The front camera moves from the short edge to the long edge, optimizing for landscape video calls.
insights.so_what: Minor design shift reflecting landscape-first tablet use.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: Only the 512GB iPad mini gets the dual 16-core Neural Engine from the iPhone 18 Pro; the 128GB and 256GB versions get a single 16-core NPU and a five-core rather than six-core CPU.
insights.so_what: Apple is beginning to segment on-device AI performance by price tier, a new upsell lever.
insights.quote: Unfortunately, not all versions of the new iPad mini will be equally capable.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam

insights.claim: For on-device AI applications, higher memory speed helps but the Neural Engine is the primary performance factor.
insights.so_what: NPU configuration, not just memory bandwidth, determines AI capability differences between SKUs.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
